hysterectomy is followed by emotional disturbances, which can be prevented by proper preoperative and postoperative psychotherapeutic support.

hysterectomy is associated with an increase in depressive reactions in women, and that this is related to the woman's attitude to the operation, the family attitudes, the woman's sexual misconceptions and her body image changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emotional disturbances following gynaecsurgical operations.
the emotional disturbances following gynecological operations and the preventive measures that can be undertaken.
the emotional disturbances of women following gynaecological operations, and the prevention of such disturbances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gynaecologist has to be aware of the emotional problems of the women undergoing gynaecologic surgery, and should be able to help them in their psychological adjustment.
the prevention of psychiatric disturbances following hysterectomy requires a multidisciplinary effort.
hysterectomy should be performed in the most favourable conditions and by the best surgeons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a hysterectomy, in itself, is not the cause of emotional disturbances, but rather a trigger for the development of such disturbances.

a woman who has a hysterectomy, if she has a good relationship with her husband, and a good body image, and if she has a positive attitude towards the operation and its consequences, will not develop psychiatric disturbances.

the emotional complications after hysterectomy can be prevented by the use of a multidisciplinary team approach, which includes the surgeon, gynaecologist, psychologist, psychiatrist, and social worker.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a woman who has had a hysterectomy should not be left to cope on her own, but instead should be given adequate psychotherapeutic and social support.

the emotional complications following gynecological operations can be prevented by proper psychological approach of patients and their relatives, adequate information about the operation, and proper psychotherapy post-operatively.
a proper approach to the woman, her family and the operation itself, can prevent the occurrence of post-operative depression and other emotional disturbances.
